newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala court jails ex-officials in 1994 killing.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala court jails ex-officials in 1994 killing.

text.p: A Guatemalan court on Thursday sentenced several former high-ranking government officials, including a former interior minister, to 10 years in prison for the 1994 police killing of a university student.

Former Interior Minister Danilo Parrinello, his top deputy Mario Alfredo Merida and the former Guatemalan police chief Salvador Figueroa were found guilty in the death of law student Alioto Lopez at the hands of anti-riot police and each sentenced to 10 years in prison.

Lopez, 19, was shot and beaten by police during a student protest over a bus fare hike in November 1994. Police officer Carlos Escobar, who was photographed kicking Lopez on the ground during the crackdown, was sentenced to 30 years.
The former officials, who served under former President Ramiro de Leon Carpio, were denied bail but can appeal their sentences, court officials said.
"Ex-minister Danilo Parrinello was condemned to 10 years in prison. The sentence is not commutable," Moises Rodriguez, an official in the Third Penal Sentencing Court, told Reuters.
The trial captured the attention of ordinary Guatemalans and symbolised a break in a tradition of impunity for government and military officials.

"For us it is highly satisfactory that the courts begin to act with liberty and autonomy from sectors that have influenced the administration of justice," the influential human rights group, the Mutual Support Group, said.

Military generals and government ministers have in the past been criminally indicted on charges they ordered assassinations during the civil war that consumed Guatemala for more than three decades until a peace treaty was signed last year.
But none of them ever stood trial, leading most citizens to believe that no government official would ever be held accountable for their actions.

A panel of three judges handed down the sentence after a week-long trial, finding the men responsible for Lopez's death because they were part of a chain of command that sent police to put down the protest.
One of the three sentencing judges dissented with his colleagues, arguing that Escobar was the only guilty party.

Former minister Parrinello and his aide Merida did not take the stand in the trial, but Escobar testified that he and fellow police officers were acting in self defence after they were injured by rock-throwing students.
A police officer also died from wounds received during the week-long bus-fare protests.
